name: Iware Supplychain Services Limited
sector: Road transportation, warehousing and multimodal logistics
summary:
Iware is a fast-expanding, road-transport-led logistics operator, not yet an evidence-backed compounder. The strongest fact is genuine pre-acquisition expansion: revenue rose from INR 24.35 crore in FY2022 to INR 85.82 crore in FY2025. The decisive constraint is turning the enlarged business into cash while paying debt, not finding an attractive headline growth rate. FY2026 revenue reached INR 257.66 crore, but the related AKT undertaking changes the perimeter and operating EBITDA margin fell to 11.29%. [S1, S2, S3, S5]

At the observed October 19 close of INR 370.35, BQS is 4.82 (display 4.8), GQS 6.25 (6.3), IAS 2.755 (2.8). A capital-constrained 5% growth base produces a funded but very thin INR 0.81 crore month-end cash trough and -3.76% five-year return; the bullish execution case gives 16.09%, but is not the central result. G3 fails the no-rescue credible-stress test, so this belongs in the funding-stressed/special-situation exclusion group, not an investable ranking. This model conclusion is not a statement of an ongoing October payment default. [S1, S6, S7, S15]

A verified improvement in collections, lender liquidity and amortization coverage, accompanied by reconciled acquired-business cash flows and improved returns on new capital, would matter more than another customer announcement. A lower share price alone cannot repair company funding.
identity_note: NSE IWARE / INE1AII01014 verified against current security master, offer document and June 5 allotment. AKT is an acquired business undertaking inside the issuer; no NCI.

quote.kind: observed official close; not live executable bid

score_note: v 3.0 exact unrounded arithmetic. G3 model-based funding failure caps IAS at 3; raw 2.755 is already below cap. No persistent-CASH/GQS cap. All numeric scores are diagnostics; failed gate excludes investable ranking.

gates.reason: RPT-heavy operations, related undertaking acquisition and disclosure discipline warrant care, but reviewed primary records do not establish severe diversion, manipulation or minority abuse. Disputed tax claims are not guilt.

Core current balance-sheet claims and signed P&L can support a conservative opening-stock model. Acquisition cash-flow separation, CARE versus annual CFO definitions and boilerplate errors remain bounded disclosure gaps; do not treat reported debt movements as pure organic cash draws. No wholesale rejection of audited earnings is justified by the evidence reviewed.

Analyst no-rescue stress, not an allegation of current default: 10% revenue loss, 9% EBITDA and roughly 11 extra net-WC days, essential maintenance and legacy claims retained, optional shed spending stopped. Cash shortfall is INR 15.68 crore; matched tax credits plus non-earmarked FD access still leave INR 5.10 crore. Even lower maintenance leaves INR 2.04 crore. Hypothetical rescue does not establish survival. Apply IAScap 3.

ST series eligible and all 60 sessions observed; theoreticalINR 5 lakh exit 2.15 days at 5% participation.600-share lot, small participant base and absent live order depth limit executability. No suspension or present exchange-default claim.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Iware is a fast-expanding, road-transport-led logistics operator, not yet an evidence-backed compounder. The strongest fact is genuine pre-acquisition expansion: revenue rose from INR 24.35 crore in FY2022 to INR 85.82 crore in FY2025. The decisive constraint is turning the enlarged business into cash while paying debt, not finding an attractive headline growth rate. FY2026 revenue reached INR 257.66 crore, but the related AKT undertaking changes the perimeter and operating EBITDA margin fell to 11.29%. [S1, S2, S3, S5]

At the observed October 19 close of INR 370.35, BQS is 4.82 (display 4.8), GQS 6.25 (6.3), IAS 2.755 (2.8). A capital-constrained 5% growth base produces a funded but very thin INR 0.81 crore month-end cash trough and -3.76% five-year return; the bullish execution case gives 16.09%, but is not the central result. G3 fails the no-rescue credible-stress test, so this belongs in the funding-stressed/special-situation exclusion group, not an investable ranking. This model conclusion is not a statement of an ongoing October payment default. [S1, S6, S7, S15]

A verified improvement in collections, lender liquidity and amortization coverage, accompanied by reconciled acquired-business cash flows and improved returns on new capital, would matter more than another customer announcement. A lower share price alone cannot repair company funding.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Cutoff: 20 October 2026, UTC; last market session 19 October, with 20 October an exchange holiday. Security: NSE EMERGE IWARE, ISIN INE1AII01014, ST series, current 11506800 issued shares. The October 19 close is INR 370.35 and current-share market capitalization INR 426.15 crore. Historical FY2026 EPS 14.37 is weighted-average, not a current-share denominator. [S1, S7, S15, S16]

Scope: standalone issuer under Indian GAAP/AS, including the purchased AKT undertaking from January 2026. No separately owned subsidiary or NCI is introduced. Units are INR crore unless specified. Scenarios run from the latest observed March 31 balance sheet, insert known dated financing/dividend events, and value an October 19, 2026 entrant through October 19, 2031. April–October cash is modeled, not observed. Default hurdle 15% nominal before personal taxes; a 12–15% nominal capital-cost range is an analyst benchmark, not the same concept. INR 5 lakh is an illustrative liquidity reference, not an allocation recommendation.

G1 Conditional: relatedness and capital discipline require monitoring; no severe integrity failure established. G2 Conditional: usable signed current stocks/earnings, but acquisition-flow and presentation limitations prevent calling all historical cash movement organic. G3 Fail—evidenced by the specific linked funding test, with IAS capped at 3. G4 Conditional: actual trading exists; lots/participants/depth constrain implementation. Detailed gate reasons and evidence are preserved in the gate register.

Confidence is High on identity, quote, current issue receipt and directly read balance-sheet line items; Medium on governance, historical cash comparability, underlying growth decomposition, capital returns and scenario inputs. Overall material confidence is Medium. Forecast uncertainty remains High and separate. No missing item is filled with a neutral 5; no factor reaches 9–10 on this history.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP 5, CASH 4, BAL 2, EXEC 5, EARN 6; IAS return R1, downside D2, expectations P2 and liquidity L6. Each has claim-linked evidence and a separate economic boundary.

BQS =1.00+0.80+0.96+0.50+0.60+0.40+0.16+0.40 =4.82. GQS =3.20+1.00+0.90+0.75+0.40 =6.25. IAS =0.25×4.82+0.35×1+0.20×2+0.10×2+0.10×6 =2.755. All have 100% factor coverage; no reweighting. Conventional half-up displays are 4.8, 6.3, 2.8, but the exact values determine classification. The G3 cap is 3 and does not further reduce this already lower IAS. No G1/governance cap or persistent-CASH/CAP growth cap is applied.

REV starts at 9 for the chosen 52.19% pre-acquisition CAGR, then caps at 8 because the relevant clean window is three years with Medium underlying-growth confidence. CASH 4 reflects severe recent weakness, not a claim that every prior year was poor. The model’s five-year base return minus 15% hurdle is -18.76 percentage points, so R1 follows the explicit schedule. [S1, S2, S3, S6]

Judgment sensitivity: moving MOAT and CAP together by ±1 changes BQS by ±0.32, GQS by ±0.15 and IAS quality contribution by ±0.08, without repairing G3. A 0.1 display difference should not be interpreted as reliable economic precision. These are policy heuristics, not validated predictors.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
The company combines road transportation, carrying/forwarding, warehousing/3 PL, rail/rake handling, auxiliary services and rental income. FY2026 road-transport lines, including separately tagged AKT road income, total INR 211.81 crore, about 82.2% of revenue. C&F contributes INR 27.64 crore, rail INR 9.87 crore and rentals INR 2.87 crore; reimbursement/miscellaneous income completes the balance. These are accounting revenue categories, not fully separable margin segments. [S1, printed 123]

It earns service fees while paying hired transport, vehicle running, handling staff and warehousing costs. FY2026 lorry hire was INR 104.66 crore and vehicle-running lines INR 86.42 crore. Thus the business mixes an owned fleet/property base with substantial subcontracted capacity; it should not be valued as either a pure software-like asset-light platform or an entirely owned-truck operator. Corporate customers can receive 60–90 day terms while suppliers offer limited credit, creating cash needs before collections. [S1, S6]

Management presents 50 operational locations and 804466+square feet under management in the detailed operating overview; broader 12 lakh-square-foot marketing language is not reconciled. The annual report refers to 165 vehicles and October CARE around 285; dates and acquired/owned/operating scope may differ. These facts establish scale and change, not verified utilization, unit margins or independently measured market share.

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Useful advantages are customer familiarity, a multi-location operating network, warehousing/rake coordination and the ability to combine hired and owned transport. Those can reduce onboarding friction for an existing client. The contrary evidence is stronger than a generic “integrated logistics” moat claim: fragmented road competition, readily available subcontractors, top-two customers accounting for 75–82% of sales over the last three years, and September arrangements without assured minimum volumes. [S1, S6, S10, S11, S12]

FY2026 operating EBITDA fell from 19.81% to 11.29% despite tripling reported revenue. Mix and expansion explain why this is not automatically a pricing collapse, but they also prevent claiming protected economics. No defensible retention-cohort, share-gain, utilization or price-premium series was available. MOAT 4 is therefore a weak/contestable-advantage judgment, not an allegation that the business lacks customers.

Three contextual comparators are Pranik Logistics, Shreeji Translogistics and VRL Logistics. The first two appear in Iware’s IPO peer section; VRL provides broader goods-network context. Their freight mix, fleet ownership, scale and capital structure differ. The prospectus’s dated FY2024/December 2024 peer figures are not current valuation evidence, and no average peer multiple is transferred to Iware. The scenario 8–12x EBIT range is an explicit analytical range, not a measured peer entitlement. [S2, S19]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Six fiscal revenue observations are INR 18.9147 crore(FY2021), 24.34632(FY2022), 43.5545(FY2023), 58.7063(FY2024), 85.8224512(FY2025) and 257.6618527(FY2026). Annual additions are 5.43162, 19.20818, 15.1518, 27.1161512 and 171.8394015 crore. FY2021/22 are original accounts, FY2023/24 restated IPO accounts, FY2025 the latest signed comparative and FY2026 the expanded issuer perimeter. [S1, S2, S3]

The primary scored window is FY2022–25, three intervals, CAGR 52.19%, selected to avoid both pandemic FY2021 and the FY2026 acquisition. The reported FY2021–26 context CAGR is 68.60% over five intervals, but is not a clean organic demand estimate. FY2022–26 is four intervals, even if a narrative source calls the five observations “five years.” No volume/fuel-price/route mix decomposition is invented.

FY2026 reported growth is 200.23%. AKT-tagged operating lines sum to INR 6.5266429 crore; subtracting only those leaves 251.1352098 crore, 192.62% above FY2025. That is a useful accounting cross-check, not proof of 192.62% organic growth: tagging and integration may not identify every acquired contract/route contribution. The acquired business’s FY2025 turnover of 76.67 crore is not its FY2026 contribution to Iware and cannot simply be subtracted. Announcement and annual effective dates differ by one day. [S1, S5]

FY2026 logistics/customer additions and September contracts support commercial access; they do not establish a guaranteed order book or six months of FY2027 realized revenue. No unavailable interim is annualized or relabeled TTM.

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The accessible opportunity is more freight per existing customer, additional routes, better warehouse utilization and new accounts such as Tube Investments, NCERT and Emami. It is not the whole national logistics TAM. C&F, rail and contracted warehousing add avenues, but demand-based volumes, short cancellation rights and the concentration of the existing book limit durability. [S1, S6, S10, S11, S12]

Funding determines which growth can create per-share value. Base assumptions deliberately restrain sales growth to 5% a year, maintaining 11.5% EBITDA and opening-scope ONWC at 20.1392% of revenue. FY2027 fresh cash capex is 10.02 crore, including 3.4911 shed completion; thereafter maintenance starts 5.5 crore and rises 5%, with growth capex equal to 8% of incremental sales. Owned fleet and subcontracting make this mix possible, but higher 15% growth-capex intensity is tested and creates a funding gap. Existing 12.21 croreCWIP transfers without being paid twice; the 0.6017 capital creditor is separately paid. [S1, S9]

An unconstrained 10% revenue-growth path at the same margin/WC policy has a 4.26 crore cash shortfall. Assuming all legally matched tax credits become usable can fund it, but the resulting 2.28% IRR remains well below 15%. This shows why historical 52% pre-acquisition CAGR cannot be mechanically extended. The bull requires 18%, 17%, 16%, 15%, 14%, 12% growth, 12%→13% margin and ONWC 19%→18%, a genuinely joint execution case rather than a free high-growth assumption.

The latest incremental capital-return proxy is 10.43%, versus 17.92% over FY2023–26. Neither proves an investment cohort’s lifetime return. CAP 5 and GQS 6.25 recognize the demand record while withholding a compounder designation until new capital produces cash and returns above the assumed 12–15% capital-cost range.

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The promoter/holding-company ecosystem supplies commercial services, related vehicles and management. FY2026 transport charges to Inter India Roadways, Edisafe Logistics, AKT Logistics LLP and United Logistics together were approximately 40.20 crore; related vehicle purchases were 3.54 crore. These are disclosed commercial transactions, not evidence of diversion. Their scale makes arm’s-length pricing and post-acquisition cash discipline important minority-shareholder questions. The 50 lakh AKT undertaking purchase was related-party; goodwill 1.9844 crore means a low purchase-price headline cannot be interpreted as free net assets. [S1, S5]

Dated promises-versus-delivery: May 2025 IPO provided 27.132 crore gross; May 12, 2026 utilization disclosed 3.4911 crore of shed allocation not yet used, citing execution/labour delays. March 13 acquisition completion was disclosed, with January 15/16 effective-date presentation differences. June 5 preferential allotment delivered actual 20.1654 crore and 790800 shares, not merely authorization. September customer arrangements were signed, but delivered volumes/profit remain to be verified. [S5, S7, S9, S10, S11, S12]

The annual audit opinion is unmodified and the secretarial report does not state an adverse qualification. Several source details nevertheless need disciplined handling: BSE versus NSE boilerplate, inconsistent IPO share wording, IndAS/NCLT references inside an AS report, and acquisition-flow classification. These do not prove fabricated earnings or fraud. Current ownership is not inferred from a stale CSV: March 31 named promoter holdings are 7856856 of 10716000 shares; June dilution is real, while an independently reconciled October beneficial-owner/pledge schedule was not obtained. [S1, S7, S16]

CARE’s October 8 rationale reports EMI delays in the twelve months ending August 2026, the last in May 2026, while assigning B+ Stable. This is not rating non-cooperation and is not proof of an ongoing October default. Annual no-default wording and the later CARE observation period need event-level reconciliation, not an accusation. Disputed income-tax/GST demands total 0.6533 crore; management disputes them and reports appeal/legal steps, with no provision. The allegation underlying a disputed demand is not adopted as proven conduct. [S1, S6]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Historical revenue/operating EBITDA/PAT/CFO, in INR crore: FY2022 24.3463/3.1651/1.1105/10.6487; FY2023 43.5545/6.2233/0.4229/2.4668; FY2024 58.7063/10.8699/4.1696/9.7384; FY2025 85.8225/17.0048/8.0193/5.9685; FY2026 257.6619/29.0833/15.0617/-19.7992. FY2021 context is separately retained. Original FY2022 cash includes 0.60 croreFD and is not mixed into a current unrestricted-cash comparison. [S1, S2, S3]

FY2026 operating EBIT is 23.6613 crore after 5.4220 depreciation; finance 4.4294, other income 0.7195 and total tax charge 4.8897 lead to PAT 15.0617. EBITDA excluding other income is 11.29% of sales, compared with 19.81% in FY2025. Normalizing operating profit after finance at 25% tax gives current-share EPS 12.54; reported weighted-average EPS 14.37 and simple current-share PAT/EPS 13.09 have different denominators/definitions. No multiple is quietly based on the most favorable EPS.

The latest signed cash statement reconciles 4.1428454 opening cash plus(-19.7991857 CFO-44.6383158 CFI+63.4981663 CFF)=3.2035102 closing cash. CFO minus 37.1555108 cash capex is -56.9546965 crore, a reported FCF proxy, not organic FCFF. CARE’s CFO-15.52 differs; it is preserved as a separate methodology/source number. May 26 revisions were described as presentation/classification changes, not a profit/assets change. Acquisition assets, liabilities and finance-cost addbacks need a separate cash bridge before organic CFO can be asserted. [S1, S4, S6]

FY2024–26 cumulative CFO/PAT is -4.0923/27.2506=-0.150x, versus 1.441x over pre-acquisition FY2023–25. The recent deterioration is significant, but one expanded-perimeter year should not erase the older record. Receivables 59.96 crore contain 20.05 crore past due, predominantly under six months; only 0.7946 crore is beyond six months. Average-balance FY2026 AR days are 52.43, closing-balance days 84.94; acquisition and growth distort comparisons, so the latter is not substituted for the former. [S1, S2]

March 31 gross debt is 70.1732 crore, not long-term 34.5454 alone: term 50.6355 already includes 16.0901 current maturities, revolver 16.3321 and demands 3.2057. Available cash 3.2035 must not be confused with 10.9019 total bank/cash including 7.6983 long-maturity FD. Gross debt/operating EBITDA is 2.41x, net available debt/EBITDA 2.30x, and EBIT/finance 5.34x, but debt-service cash headroom is much tighter than those ratios imply. [S1, S6]

Opening ONWC 51.8911 includes AR, supplier/employee/GST/other operating advances and accrued income, minus AP, all 7.2618 statutory/operating current liabilities and 1.9166 salary/audit/expense provisions. Income-tax/TDS/TCS credits 6.3659 are excluded from WC and only used in named alternatives. Existing taxes 5.1509, gratuity 0.1262 and CWIP creditor 0.6017 are paid once on dated schedules. Noncurrent gratuity 0.852935 and customer deposit 0.20214 remain terminal claims or are paid in sensitivity. RPT salary/remuneration balances are components of the existing provisions, not extra liabilities. DTA, operating deposits and related-party/interest receivables receive no free-cash windfall. This is the research model’s classification, not a correction of issuer accounting.

The capital proxy equity+debt-cash-FD grows 30.3656→30.9249→41.6800→114.9941 crore from FY2023 to FY2026. Normalized 25% tax NOPAT yields FY2026 average-capital ROIC 22.65%, one-year increment 10.43% and three-year increment 17.92%; timing, acquisition and immature CWIP limit precision. The complete financial and claim ledgers retain formulas and individual components.

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Observed equity capitalization is INR 426.1543 crore. Using the March 31 available-cash/debt bridge, EV is 493.1240 crore, P/E28.29x, EV/operating EBITDA 16.96x and P/B 7.65x. This is a mixed-date cross-check explicitly labeled as such, not a claim to observed October net debt. June equity cash enters the dated model and is not also deducted a second time from historical EV. Negative FY2026 FCF makes a simple positive FCF-yield valuation inappropriate. [S1, S7, S15]

The primary intrinsic-return method values annualized terminal EBIT and then deducts remaining debt, legacy gratuity and customer deposits, adding only accumulated free cash. Terminal multiple is 10x base, 12x bull and 7x bear. Leases/hire costs remain in operating expense under the disclosed AS accounts; no invented IFRS 16 lease liability is added. All cash interest is funded on average modeled debt. No future discretionary dividends are assumed; the already-declared FY2026 dividend leaves company cash but belongs to pre-July 31 holders, not an October entrant.

Base: 5% growth, 11.5% EBITDA, unchanged 20.1392% ONWC/sales; terminal annualized revenue 345.29 crore, EBIT 32.22, EV 322.19, cash 47.08, debt 16.33, legacy claims 1.0551, equity 351.88 crore, terminal price 305.81. Five-year IRR-3.76%, minimum month-end cash 0.81 crore. Base liquidity depends on revolver renewal and eligible access to earmarked shed funds, not additional financing.

Bull: 18%→12% growth, 12%→13% margin, ONWC 19%→18%, 12x EBIT; terminal price 780.90, IRR 16.09%, minimum cash 2.00. Bear without rescue is not funded and receives no investor IRR. A separate 20 crore rescue in April 2027 at 185/share with 3% fees adds 0.108108 crore shares; if available on time, terminal price 121.70 and IRR-19.96%. This conditional transaction is not committed or forecast as certain.

Two-way 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% growth versus 8x, 10x, 12x EBIT sensitivity reruns cash, not just EPS. At the base margin/unchanged WC, no funded 15% hurdle point appears in the 0–40% growth grid; maximum funded constant growth is 5.8%. Faster growth can reduce feasibility because it consumes cash before term amortization ends. The base terminal value supports entry prices 173.54/152.05/133.69 at 12%/15%/18% hurdles, before friction. These are conditional model prices, not “buy below” instructions while G3 fails.

Separate tests cover early WC build, tax-credit matching/delay, inaccessible cash in hand, FD lock, higher capital intensity, extra 5 crorecompletion spending, legacy/contingent settlements and revolving-facility nonrenewal. Each unfunded path has IRR null. A 1% entry and 1% exit friction sensitivity reduces the base return to approximately-4.14%; actual spreads/impact are unknown. No scenario probabilities are invented.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The key thesis -break variable is cash generated after working-capital and mandatory debt service. A large customer reducing volume can lower asset utilization/margin while collection slows and debt amortization continues. Existing 60–90 day terms, top-two 75–82% concentration, high CC use and CARE’s historical EMI-delay disclosure make this a credible linked risk rather than a remote universal catastrophe. [S1, S6]

The main stress takes a 10% first-year revenue fall, 9% EBITDA margin, and three percentage points more ONWC/revenue, approximately 11 additional net-working-capital days. It does not stack a receivable write-off on that delay. Optional shed expansion stops; its 3.4911 earmark remains reserved, not freely released. Maintenance, current taxes/benefits, ordinary statutory/supplier obligations, the capital creditor, term amortization and interest continue. The minimum cash shortfall is 15.68 crore, first arising 2027-05-31. No negative-cash path is assigned a realizable target price or shareholder IRR.

Countercases are not hidden: full matched tax-credit realization cuts the gap to 9.31; adding possible access to the 4.2072 crore non-earmarked FD portion reduces it to 5.10; reducing annual maintenance to 4.5 still leaves 2.04. The same adverse volume/margin path without additional collection drag, with favorable tax/FD access, is near the boundary at 0.24 crore. Better customer retention/margins, genuine bank headroom, slower contractual amortization or funded operating improvement could therefore change the gate. The model does not claim those alternatives are impossible.

A severe 25% customer-volume case with nonrenewal is additionally unfunded; it is a boundary test, not a probability-weighted central forecast. A conditional rescue can preserve operations but dilutes shareholders and still produces a weak return. Impairment risk is High: current holders can lose through economic deterioration, financing terms and an expensive entry, not merely a quoted drawdown. CARE B+ Stable and no verified current October default remain explicit counterevidence to describing the issuer as presently in default.

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A tenfold price in five years requires 58.49% annual growth in price; 5×requires 37.97%. Those are shareholder outcomes, not interchangeable with sales growth. At unchanged current shares and no new dividends, 5×/10×require equity values approximately 2130.77/4261.54 crore, versus 426.15 today. At a 12x terminal EBIT multiple with neutral net cash/debt, that implies roughly 177.56/355.13 croreEBIT. At 10% EBIT margin the revenue order of magnitude is 1775.64/3551.29 crore, before extra financing/legacy claims.

Neither magnitude follows from today’s demand-based customer contracts. The funded bull terminal price around 780.90 is only 2.11×the entry price over five years, and already requires margin and WC improvement plus continued growth. Claiming 5×/10×would require a much stronger financed route/customer/capital-return bridge and likely further share dilution. Classification: speculative/unsupported on current evidence, not mathematically impossible. The short test is included for perspective, not a long-range target.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Eight company-specific items are retained in the structured monitoring register: cash realization, debt servicing, customer/receivable concentration, margin/capital returns, AKT/RPT integration, shed/equity utilization, new-contract delivery, and practical liquidity/disclosure consistency. Baselines, expected improvements, investigation warnings and genuine thesis -break thresholds are separate. In particular, CARE’s historical delays are not a new default alert; each subsequent fact needs its own date and resolution status.

The review cadence is tied to the next signed half/full-year statements, rating/material-event filings and any contemplated implementation. This is a research checklist only. It is not a recurring monitoring service or instruction to trade, contact the issuer or act on an unverified alarm.

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
BQS 4.82 and IAS 2.755 would ordinarily fall in “Weak setup / value-trap risk”; the prior G3 failure takes precedence: “Distressed / funding failure—scenario-based funding stress, not a claim of current default.” This is a speculative, capital-constrained logistics expansion story, not an evidence-backed compounder. GOV 5/MOAT 4/DUR 5/CAP 5 and BAL 2 independently fail the compounder criteria even though the pre-acquisition growth record is strong.

Action category: avoid eligibility for a new investment on the assessed evidence; continue research on funding, collections and capital returns. This is not a sell instruction for an unknown existing holding and not a portfolio allocation. In batch presentation, keep the record in the gate-excluded group; retain all three numeric diagnostics without letting GQS 6.25 make it look investable.

What could change it: credible committed liquidity matched to maturities; a verified cash/debt roll-forward after June equity; reconciled acquired-business cash flows; sustained 11–12% margin with working-capital improvement; and diversified delivered customer revenue. The conditional 15% hurdle entry estimate near 152 is not a purchase recommendation while essential-funding resilience remains unresolved. A share-price decline does not inject operating cash.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence consists of the FY2026 annual signed statements/notes, the final IPO prospectus/restated FY2023–25 accounts, original FY2022 accounts, revised May 26 results, AKT acquisition disclosure, actualJune allotment/objects, IPO utilization, August AGM voting, September contracts, October CARE rationale and dated NSE market files. Every material input links to evidence and exact source locators; the source ledger distinguishes fully read material from scanned/partial records. No undated intake CSV is treated as current proof.

Important reconciliations:FY2025 original/restated cash includes FD differently; latest annual comparative controls current CF analysis. CARE CFO and PBILDT definitions differ from operating EBITDA/latest CFO and are retained separately. Acquisition-date and bookkeeping tags do not establish a complete organic bridge. Original FY2022 tables use rupees in hundreds. Current 11506800 shares differ from annual weighted-average EPS shares. NSE eligible ST/price-discovery status is not suspension. Drafting and model assumptions do not constitute issuer accounting corrections.

Open questions are specific rather than blanket missingness: current bank cash and available sanctioned headroom; contractual post-March amortization after all acquired loans; acquired cash/debt/WC bridge; legal/timingmatch for tax credits; bank-specificFD restrictions; actual shed commissioning and final cost; account-level sales/volume/price and client concentration; updated beneficial ownership/pledge; final tax-appeal outcomes. These do not justify inventing cash or calling fraud, but they constrain confidence and favorable investment conclusions.

Dominant analyst assumptions are operating margin, WC stock/timing, essential maintenance, term repayment schedule, revolver renewal, authorized FD access, no additional central fundraise and 8–12x terminal EBIT. All severe/alternative paths retain opening claims, financing costs and dilution. Forecast uncertainty is high; numeric precision describes calculation, not knowledge of future prices.

GOV.reason: An audited, disclosed capital-raising and operating record supports an adequate baseline. Family/holding-company commercial dependence, the related undertaking purchase and imprecise disclosures limit confidence in disciplined minority-value allocation. No substantiated diversion or severe minority abuse was identified; tax disputes and RPTs are not automatically misconduct.

MOAT.reason: Service capability, existing relationships and a multimodal footprint are useful but contestable. Very high concentration, short demand-based contracts, subcontractor dependence and margin compression do not demonstrate durable switching costs or a structural cost moat.

REV.reason: Choose pre-acquisition FY2022–25 before seeing the scoring outcome: 52.19% CAGR starts at 9. The three-year/Medium-confidence ceiling makes 8, with no further trajectory bonus. FY2026 reported 200.23% growth is shown separately; tagged AKT lines are not a complete organic bridge, and pandemic FY2021 is not used to inflate the score.

DUR.reason: Road/rail logistics demand and verified new account access create runway, but top-two concentration, cancellable one-year arrangements and financial capacity materially constrain accessible duration. Broad sector size is not booked work.

CAP.reason: Three-year incremental NOPAT/capital proxy 17.92% is encouraging, while latest-year 10.43% falls below the assumed 12–15% capital-cost range. New fleet/CWIP and acquisition timing may mature, but do not yet prove superior returns on fresh capital. Mixed evidence supports 5, not a neutral placeholder.

CASH.reason: FY2024–26 reported CFO/PAT is -0.150x and FY2026 required material funding. Prior pre-acquisition FY2023–25 conversion 1.441x and acquisition-stock contamination prevent labeling this as persistent proven cash destruction. No GQS persistent-CASH cap is applied; current realization remains weak.

BAL.reason: Known equity helps, but a carefully restrained credible stress cannot meet essential claims without uncommitted funding, even with favorable credit/deposit realization alternatives. Base month-end cushion is under 1 crore and actual historical servicing delays reinforce fragility. No current October default is asserted.

EXEC.reason: Substantial sales/fleet expansion, completed acquisition and signed customer additions demonstrate capability. Shed delay, margin compression, and unresolved acquired-flow integration prevent a high repeatability score; an order announcement is not delivered economic profit.

EARN.reason: PAT expansion is principally operating rather than other-income driven, and current-share EPS remains above FY2025. However 19.8%→11.3% operating EBITDA compression, acquisition contribution, a non-operating gain and fresh dilution weaken per-share persistence. CASH is judged separately.

R.reason: Supported capital-constrained base IRR-3.758% is 18.758 percentage points below the 15% hurdle, putting R in the <−10 pp band. A conditional bull is not substituted for the base to raise the score.

D.reason: Credible linked stress requires recapitalization; conditional 20 crore equity at 185 with 3% fees yields about-19.96% annualized to current holders. Unfunded cases have no shareholder IRR. The recovery path is highly funding-dependent.

P.reason: The 426.15 crore equity price embeds continued profitable scaling while historical cash/debt-service constraints restrict it. No fully funded 15% hurdle crossing exists in the base 11.5% margin/no-efficiency 0–40% growth grid at 8–12x EBIT; improved margins, WC and execution must arrive together.

L.reason: 60-day theoretical 2.15-day exit starts at 7. One-point disclosed downgrade reflects 600-share/INR 2.22 lakh lots and thin participant/caution evidence. No observed spread/depth data to justify an upper-band score; not automatically NS for unavailable live order book.

monitoring_plan.milestone: Separate acquired revenue/assets/liabilities/cash bridge and arm’s-length evidence
monitoring_plan.warning: Further related deals without consideration/cash-return transparency
monitoring_plan.thesis_break: Substantiated material minority harm, not relatedness alone
monitoring_plan.timing: Next audited notes and material acquisition filings

monitoring_plan.milestone: Dated completion/use evidence with matched authorized spending and cash
monitoring_plan.warning: Another completion delay or material unbudgetedcost
monitoring_plan.thesis_break: Documented unauthorized diversion or essential funding failure
monitoring_plan.timing: Next utilization report and audited capital notes

monitoring_plan.milestone: Actual revenue, contribution, repeat volumes and timely collections
monitoring_plan.warning: Announcements without disclosed delivery or margin evidence
monitoring_plan.thesis_break: Termination of a material account with no replacement economics
monitoring_plan.timing: Next result/disclosure; do not treat contract value as guaranteed

monitoring_plan.milestone: Observed stable depth/trading and reconciliation of current capital/financial presentation
monitoring_plan.warning: One-sided circuits, stale quote or large unreconciled capital/cash changes
monitoring_plan.thesis_break: Confirmed untradeability or material financial unreliability
monitoring_plan.timing: Before any implementation decision, not an automatic trading alert
